guide: Open Start and type your imprint name and your own numbers in the yellow cells: the direct share goal, payment fee, shipping, postage, the print margin you want and the profit per hour you want at an event.
Check Team, Stores, Countries and Formats once. Team holds the phones for the message links; Countries holds the sales tax percent (an estimate, confirm with your adviser).
Keep Editions up to date: list price, direct price, print or delivery cost, royalty share and pages. Every margin sheet reads these.

Write each direct order in Direct Orders and the monthly totals with your total revenue in Direct Income by Month. The net, fee share and direct share fill in; Direct Share Goal shows 12 months against your goal.
Direct Margin by Edition and Print Cost and Margin show the net per copy, the lowest price and a verdict for every edition. Write the date you checked each price in the yellow column.
Write every order in from the printer, every copy sold at an event, given away or lost in Stock Movements. Stock Position adds them up, values them at cost and says reprint now or wait.
Write each event in Events and its sale lines in Event Sale Lines. Event Profit ranks the events by profit per hour, and Event Kinds shows which kind of event to do more of.
Write each rights deal in Rights Deals and each payment in Rights Instalments, as status and amounts only. Rights Income by Month shows what is due, received and still open.
Use the 18 calculators to judge a price, plan a print order, check a count, decide a reprint, book or skip an event, review a rights offer and forecast the next 6 months.

Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists, tap a message link to send a ready text. One to three books: use the direct and print margin and event profit with a few rows. Figures are estimates.

listing.title: Author and Self-Publisher Direct Sales, Stock, Events and Rights Excel Template: Direct Margin, Print Margin, Event Profit, Rights Ledger
listing.headline: Know what your direct store, stock, events and rights deals really earn
listing.description:
Run the four income lines an author handles by hand in one Excel workbook. Built for an independent author who publishes under one or two pen names, sells from a direct store, hand-sells printed copies at events and keeps a few rights deals. Direct Orders and Direct Income by Month show the net of every order after the payment fee and delivery cost, with sales tax collected kept out of income. Direct Margin by Edition sets each edition against the same edition in a store and gives the lowest price that holds your net. Direct Share Goal tracks the share of your income that comes from the direct store against your own goal.

Print Cost and Margin works out the print cost by page count, the royalty a store pays, the cost of an author copy and the margin when you sell it by hand, with the minimum price. Stock Movements and Stock Position keep a ledger of copies in, sold, given and lost, with the value at cost, a reorder point from your own sales and a reprint verdict. Events and Event Profit give the profit and the profit per hour of every fair, market, talk and signing, rank them in your own history and say go again, go again with changes or skip. Rights Deals, Rights Instalments and Rights Income by Month keep translation, audio and other deals as status and amounts: fee, agent share, effective income per year, payments due in 90 days and term ends.

18 calculators cover the direct margin, the price solver, the share goal, moving copies to your direct store, print margin, author copy cost, minimum print price, stock count, reorder and reprint, event profit, go or skip, kind ranking, the packing list, the rights ledger, payments due, expiry watch, offer review and a 6-month forecast. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to the assistant, web developer, accountant, printer, event organiser, rights agent, translator and the author.

This is part seven of the Author and Self-Publisher Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Figures are estimates until the payment arrives, and every price, share, fee and target is your own number: check each store's current terms and confirm tax and contract matters with your adviser. It helps you keep track and does not promise sales.
